name: Durban masala fried fish
summary: Hake fillets rubbed with a red masala, lemon and garlic paste and pan-fried until crisp at the edges, the Durban Friday-night fish.
about: In Durban's Indian homes, fish is often on the table on a Friday, and the quickest way to cook it is to rub it with the same chilli-red masala used for curry and fry it. Hake is the fish most South African families buy; it takes the spice well and flakes beautifully. It is eaten with rice, a tomato and onion salad or tucked into a soft roll.

ingredients.name: Fresh coriander
ingredients.note: finely chopped, plus extra to serve

steps: Pat the hake dry with paper towel. Mix the masala, turmeric, ground coriander and cumin, ginger and garlic paste, salt, lemon juice and chopped coriander into a thick red paste.
Rub the paste all over the fish and leave it on a plate for 10 minutes while the pan heats (or up to 2 hours, covered, in the fridge).
Heat the oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Add the curry leaves, if using, and let them crackle for a few seconds.

Lay half the fish in the pan and fry without moving it for 3 minutes, until a dark red crust forms underneath. Turn carefully with a spatula and fry for 2–3 minutes more, until the fish is white all the way through and flakes when pressed with a fork. Keep warm while you fry the second batch.
Serve hot with lemon wedges, extra coriander, rice and a tomato, onion and chilli salad.
prepNote: Rub the fish with the masala paste up to 2 hours ahead and keep it covered in the fridge.
